finding: src/anomaly/acquire.py:46 Direct source registration can follow an existing in-case symlink and overwrite another case artifact.
rationale: The finding survives because this mainline registration entry calls only unscanned case/document validation, resolves an in-case destination symlink to its artifact target, and writes payload bytes to that resolved target; neither its decorator nor an upstream guard makes the overwrite unreachable or fail-safe.

evidence.output: register_local_source calls resume_case(root) and validate_case_documents(root), builds relative = data/raw/<source_id>/<source-name>, and sets dest = _under_root(root, relative). _under_root computes candidate = (base / relative).resolve(), rejects only candidates outside base, and returns an in-case resolved candidate. For a new included source, lines 128-129 execute dest.parent.mkdir(...) and dest.write_bytes(payload), so a destination symlink resolving to case.json causes the CSV payload to be written to case.json.

evidence.output: case.py:146-150 resume_case only checks _case_exists and calls _load_case; it does not call _scan_case_tree. semantics.py:180-225 validate_case_documents reads data/sources.json and scans only .anomaly/receipts. events.py:51-67 phase_event merely calls the wrapped function and logs success/failure. workflow.py:102-113 does scan in run_workflow, but that guard belongs only to that separate wrapper and does not precede a direct register_local_source call.
